parts.label: Part 1
parts.article:
Hello, Winsham Farm Centre.

Oh, hello. I want to arrange a weekend away for myself and some people from work, and we heard about your centre. I wonder if you could give me some details.

Yes, certainly. We are a residential centre attached to a working farm, and we organise educational activities for those guests who want them. What else would you like to know?

Well, firstly, what kind of accommodation have you got?

We’ve got eight rooms altogether, and we can sleep 38 at any one time. Three of the rooms have got six bunks, and five of them have got four bunks.

Right, and what other facilities are there?

We have separate toilets and showers for each of the rooms. There’s a large dining room and a large meeting room, which can be booked by groups in advance, but I’m afraid we had a flood in there last month, and the floor was slightly damaged, so unfortunately it’s out of use just now. We’ve got workmen coming in next week. When were you thinking of staying?

In three weeks time, the 28th of September.

Oh, it should be okay by then.

Oh, well, that’s okay then. And what about food? Do you provide meals or is it self-catering?

We’re very flexible. As long as you give us enough notice, we can cater for you, or if you prefer, you can just bring your own food and use the kitchen facilities. And some people prefer to eat out, which is also fine.

Fine, and I heard that your farm is organic. Does that mean that you only have crops and no animals?

It doesn’t actually. A lot of people seem to think that, but we do rear livestock as well. And so we have a wide range of food. Organic means it’s all produced without the use of artificial fertilizers or pesticides.

I see, that sounds good. Could you tell me what sort of recreational activities are available, either at the centre or in the area?

Yes. Here at the centre, we offer farm tours. They’re very popular. One of the farm managers shows people around and explains some of the principles of organic farming. And for any visitors who are really keen, we let them drive a tractor or feed the animals and so on, with supervision, of course.

I think a lot of our group would be interested in that. It’d make a change from factory work.

Well, if they fancy it, tell them to come prepared. Plenty of old clothing. Especially footwear. It can be very messy and wet.

OK, I’ll warn them.

And another type of activity we do is survival courses, but that’s only for groups of five or more. And they’ve got to be acquaintances. They have to co-operate closely. These courses are very popular, especially with school groups, but adults seem to enjoy them too.

What do they involve? Things like map reading?

Well, not exactly. What it is, we’ve got a large area of woodland on the farm, and we run this course there. It’s mainly about collecting food and water, lighting a fire without any equipment. That kind of thing. This weekend could be hard work.

What about the area around the centre? What is there to do?

If you look at a map, you’ll see that we’re very well situated here. Our centre’s about midway between the Exmoor National Park, which is very popular for hill walking, and the South Coast, which has very good beaches.

Are they both within walking distance?

Well, they’re both a bit far, unless you’re very fit. But they’re only about 30 minutes by road, and there’s also a cycle path, which starts quite near here, about 10 minutes walk away. You can hire bikes at the starting point.

What is there to do if the weather’s bad? I hope it won’t be, but you never know.

Yes, that’s right. Well, on most Saturday evenings, we show films here, and then, once a month, a group of local musicians performs in our meeting room. And then, Sherborne is only 14 miles away. It’s only a small town, but it’s got a very good museum, and an old abbey, which is well worth a visit.

Well, it sounds perfect for our purposes. One last thing, what about prices? I’m not sure yet, but they’ll probably be about 15 of us.

We charge a standard £14 a head for accommodation, whether there are 10 or 20 of you or whatever; and about £7 for cooked meals, depending on the menu you want. Use of the kitchen facilities is extra, as is the hire of the meeting room. It depends, really, what exactly you want, and for how many people.

Right. Well, I’ve made a note of all that, and I’ll discuss it with the rest of the group. Then I’ll get back to you with a firm booking. Can I do that by phone?

Yes, you can. But once you’ve made a booking, we would need a deposit within five days to secure it. Then you just pay the balance when you’re here.

Oh, yes, of course. Could you give me the address, please?

Yes. It’s Winsham Farm, Cotehele Road, that’s C-O-T-E-H-E-L-E, near Sherborne. And the postcode is SH121LQ.

Thank you.

questions.question: The centre has enough accommodation for

analyses.content: 录音中明确提到中心一共有8个房间，任何时候都可以睡 38 人（sleep 38 at any one time），直接对应选项 C。
We’ve got eight rooms altogether, and we can sleep 38 at any one time.
不要被后面的“3个房间有6张床”或“5个房间有4张床”等细节数字干扰，题目问的是总容量。
...but I’m afraid we had a flood in there last month, and the floor was slightly damaged, so unfortunately it’s out of use just now.
选项 B (flooded) 是上个月发生的原因（had a flood last month），题目问的是当前的状态（currently），现在状态是“坏了/不能用”，而不是正在发大水。
录音说会议室上个月发大水，地板坏了，所以不幸的是目前 out of use（无法使用），对应选项 A（unavailable）。

questions.question: Visitors must tell the centre in advance if they want to

analyses.content: As long as you give us enough notice, we can cater for you...
自己带食物（self-catering）或去外面吃（eat out）都被描述为 flexible 的选项，并没有提到需要“提前通知”。
录音提到只要你给我们 enough notice（足够的提前通知），我们可以为你 cater（提供餐饮/做饭），这对应选项 B。

questions.question: All visitors on the tour of the farm can

analyses.content: One of the farm managers shows people around and explains some of the principles of organic farming.
选项 B 和 C（喂动物、开拖拉机）录音明确说是针对 visitors who are really keen（特别感兴趣的游客），而不是题目问的 All visitors。
录音说农场经理会带大家参观并解释 principles of organic farming（有机农业的原则），这是针对 people（大家）的通用活动。

questions.question: On the survival course people have to

analyses.content: It’s mainly about collecting food and water, lighting a fire without any equipment.
录音明确否定了 map reading（Wait, not exactly），而 run through woodland 是活动发生的地点背景，不是核心任务。
关于生存课程，录音说主要是关于在没有设备的情况下 collecting food（收集食物），这对应选项 B（找到他们自己的食物）。

questions.question: From the centre it is easy to walk to

analyses.content: 录音提到有一条 cycle path（自行车道）起始于离这里仅 10 minutes walk（步行10分钟）的地方，符合题干 easy to walk to。
...and there’s also a cycle path, which starts quite near here, about 10 minutes walk away.
国家公园和海滩（Exmoor / South Coast）录音都说 a bit far（有点远），除非你非常健壮，否则步行很难到达（需开车30分钟）。

questions.question: If the weather is bad, visitors can go to a

analyses.content: It’s only a small town, but it’s got a very good museum, and an old abbey, which is well worth a visit.
录音虽然提到了 show films，但那是直接在中心（here）播放的，不是去外面的 cinema（电影院）。
录音说附近的 Sherborne 镇虽然小，但有一个很好的 museum（博物馆）值得参观。

questions.question: Group who wish to stay at the centre must pay

analyses.content: But once you’ve made a booking, we would need a deposit within five days to secure it. Then you just pay the balance when you’re here.
听到 balance（余款）要反应过来这是指剩下的钱，说明不需要一开始就付 all of the cost。
预定后需要在五天内支付 deposit（定金），余款（balance）到了再付，定金即“部分费用”。

groups.contentHtml:
Address: Winsham Farm Road Near Sherborne
Postcode:

analyses.content: It’s Winsham Farm, Cotehele Road, that’s C-O-T-E-H-E-L-E, near Sherborne.
拼写中包含不发音字母或易混淆元音，需紧跟录音节奏，千万不要漏掉中间的 H 或结尾的 E。
录音中提到路名后，紧接着进行了逐字母拼写 C-O-T-E-H-E-L-E，直接对应题干中 ....... Road 前的空缺。
And the postcode is SH121LQ.
雅思听力中的邮编常考察“字数混合”，一定要区分清楚数字 1 (one) 和字母 L (el) 的发音区别。
听到提示词 Postcode（邮编）后，录音清晰报出了一串由字母和数字组成的编码 SH12 1LQ。
